factual_methodological.summary: INE final Q2 2026 national accounts revision, labour and population releases, Banco de España external/debt data and current housing-policy context were checked against official sources.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: The report distinguishes strong aggregate growth from per-capita productivity, housing, regional and fiscal constraints and does not infer structural convergence from cyclical outperformance.

novelty_against_existing_country_layer.summary: No canonical Spain country-context dossier exists; the report adds reusable context on migration-led labour supply, housing, renewables, European investment, regional institutions and external balances.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Both locales contain one table, five charts and a structural flow with semantic and numerical parity.

political_neutrality.summary: Institutions, governments and territorial politics are described analytically without partisan or electoral endorsement.

contrary_evidence: Rapid employment, population and investment growth provide real resilience rather than merely statistical noise.
A current-account surplus and improving net international investment position reduce external vulnerability even as domestic demand leads growth.
Renewable expansion and infrastructure investment can raise productive capacity, while interconnection and housing constraints can still bind.
limitations: Quarterly GDP and labour data remain revisable even after the September national-accounts update.
Population estimates are provisional and migration-flow measures use distinct statistical concepts.
Observed debt ratios and annual institutional forecasts use different denominators and horizons.
notes: Approved after primary-source verification current to 4 October 2026, bilingual parity review, controlled-taxonomy review and visual-evidence review.

en.title: Spain: immigration-led expansion, renewable power and the productivity test after NextGenerationEU
en.deck: Spain is outperforming the euro area through immigration, employment and investment while reducing external and fiscal vulnerabilities; the structural test is whether renewable electricity, housing reform and EU-financed investment translate into lasting productivity gains.
en.regime: Fast-growing euro-area economy supported by immigration, domestic demand and EU-financed investment, with improving external balances and debt ratios but persistent productivity, housing, unemployment and ageing constraints.
en.key_risk: Growth slows sharply after NextGenerationEU and migration normalisation if productivity, firm scaling and housing supply fail to improve enough to sustain per-capita income convergence.

pt-BR.title: Espanha: expansão apoiada pela imigração, eletricidade renovável e o teste de produtividade após o NextGenerationEU
pt-BR.deck: A Espanha supera a área do euro com imigração, emprego e investimento enquanto reduz vulnerabilidades externas e fiscais; o teste estrutural é transformar eletricidade renovável, reforma habitacional e investimento europeu em ganhos permanentes de produtividade.
pt-BR.regime: Economia da área do euro em crescimento rápido, sustentada por imigração, demanda doméstica e investimento financiado pela UE, com melhora das contas externas e da dívida, mas restrições persistentes de produtividade, habitação, desemprego e envelhecimento.
pt-BR.key_risk: O crescimento desacelera fortemente após o NextGenerationEU e a normalização migratória caso produtividade, crescimento das empresas e oferta habitacional não melhorem o suficiente para sustentar convergência da renda por habitante.

publication.selection_rationale: Spain is one of the largest euro-area and NATO economies but the public corpus lacks reusable country-level context on its post-2008 institutional transformation, immigration-led labour expansion, housing constraints, tourism system, renewable-electricity advantage, regional state, industrial base and NextGenerationEU transition. Existing European security and major-country research require this context to analyse EU growth, energy, defence burden-sharing and Mediterranean transmission without rebuilding the same structural mechanisms.
contrary_evidence: Strong GDP, employment, current-account performance and a falling debt ratio argue against a renewed euro-crisis narrative, while weak productivity, high unemployment and ageing argue against treating recent outperformance as a solved convergence problem.
Rapid immigration increases labour supply and fiscal revenue, but housing scarcity and low-productivity employment can reduce the gain in GDP per capita if capital and infrastructure do not adjust.
Renewables already dominate annual electricity generation, but Spain remains exposed to oil, gas, transport fuels and limited interconnection with continental Europe.
Tourism is a major service export and regional income source, while local congestion and housing competition show that its benefits and costs are geographically uneven.
limitations: 2026 population and migration figures are provisional and citizenship, birthplace and residence are different statistical measures.
Quarterly observed debt ratios and annual institutional forecasts use different denominators and timing and should not be treated as the same observation.
Spain's Recovery and Resilience Plan has been revised repeatedly; this dossier uses the current European Commission allocation rather than older maximum envelopes.
Housing-market conditions vary strongly by municipality and autonomous community and national averages can obscure local scarcity.
Installed renewable capacity does not equal usable annual generation because storage, transmission and interconnection constrain integration.
Tourism expenditure is a gross export receipt and is not identical to domestic value added.
NATO defence-spending ratios depend on accounting definitions and the separation between core defence and wider security-related expenditure.
